title: Differentially verify C and Rust program behavior
summary: For each agreed reproducible behavior of an authorized C-to-Rust port, run the original C baseline and Rust implementation with equivalent inputs and relevant environment, compare observable outputs, exit codes and side effects, and document any intentionally accepted differences.
statement: For each agreed reproducible behavior of an authorized C-to-Rust port, run the original C baseline and Rust implementation with equivalent inputs and relevant environment, compare observable outputs, exit codes and side effects, and document any intentionally accepted differences.
rationale: Running equivalent cases against the upstream implementation reveals behavioral divergences that normal unit tests may miss. Record nondeterministic output normalization and untestable cases explicitly.

conditions: An authorized C-to-Rust port has an agreed upstream baseline and equivalent test cases are runnable or reference observations are available.
exceptions: Documented accepted deviations and justified nondeterministic differences; missing baseline executability must be reported as a verification gap, not silently treated as a passing test.
